sites.name: Christ the Redeemer
sites.fact: A 30-metre statue on top of Corcovado, 700 metres above the city. It was completed in 1931.
sites.hint: On the sharp summit in the middle of the city: climb to reach it.

sites.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
sites.fact: A 396-metre granite peak at the mouth of the bay. A cable car has run to the top since 1912.
sites.hint: The bare rock dome at the entrance to the bay.

sites.name: Copacabana Beach
sites.fact: Four kilometres of sand in a long curve. The wave pattern in the pavement beside it is a design from Portugal.
sites.hint: The long curved beach south of Sugarloaf.

sites.name: Ipanema Beach
sites.fact: The beach that gave the song its name. The twin peaks of Dois Irmãos stand at its western end.
sites.hint: The straight beach west of Copacabana, in front of the lagoon.

sites.name: Maracanã Stadium
sites.fact: Opened for the 1950 World Cup, whose final drew a crowd of almost 200,000, a record for football.
sites.hint: The big oval stadium north-west of the centre.

sites.name: Sambadrome
sites.fact: A 700-metre parade avenue with stands on both sides, designed by Oscar Niemeyer and opened in 1984 for the Carnival samba parades.
sites.hint: A straight strip lined with grandstands, west of the centre.

sites.name: Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon
sites.fact: A saltwater lagoon linked to the sea by a canal, with a path about 7.5 kilometres long around it.
sites.hint: The lagoon behind Ipanema, under Corcovado.

sites.name: Santos Dumont Airport
sites.fact: The city airport, on land reclaimed from the bay and named for Brazil's aviation pioneer. Its runway is only about 1,300 metres long.
sites.hint: The short runway sticking into the bay beside the centre.

sites.name: Rio–Niterói Bridge
sites.fact: More than 13 kilometres long, it crosses Guanabara Bay. It opened in 1974.
sites.hint: The long bridge across the bay, north of the centre.

sites.name: Tijuca Forest
sites.fact: One of the largest urban forests in the world, replanted by hand from the 1860s after coffee farming had stripped the hills.
sites.hint: The forested mountains west of Corcovado.

sites.name: Pedra da Gávea
sites.fact: A granite mountain 844 metres high that rises almost straight from the ocean.
sites.hint: The flat-topped rock above the coast, west of Ipanema.

sites.name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum
sites.fact: Oscar Niemeyer's saucer-shaped museum, opened in 1996 on a cliff across the bay from Rio.
sites.hint: On a point on the far side of the bay, east of the city airport.
